dedupe_keys.name: china national green data centre lists 国家绿色数据中心名单

description: China's Ministry of Industry and Information Technology, with five other national bodies, selects and publishes each year a list of national green data centres, facilities judged to lead on energy efficiency, green power use, water saving and sustainable operation. Candidates are nominated by provinces, reviewed by experts and publicly announced for comment before the final list is issued, and power usage effectiveness (PUE) carries the greatest weight in the evaluation. The 2021 list named 44 data centres run by telecom operators, internet companies and others, the 2023 list named 50, and the 2025 draft list was published for comment from 28 October to 3 November 2025. The lists accompany national targets: new large and very large data centres should reach a PUE of 1.25 or less by the end of 2025, and projects at national computing hub nodes 1.2 or less, against a national average PUE reported at about 1.48 to 1.52 in 2021 to 2023; the 43 green data centres of 2022 averaged 1.27. Coverage: China, annual lists since about 2017. Format and access: announcements with list attachments on ministry websites, free. Caveats: lists name exemplary sites only and may not give each site's measured PUE; attachments are in Chinese. Simulation uses: efficiency benchmarks and locations of major Chinese data centres for energy demand models, and context on policy targets. Related records: the EU data centre energy performance database and Germany's register are the European counterparts.
